arguments.prompt: Head-height medium shot from the wet paving in front of the left end of a long finished timber stage, looking straight at City Hall; the stage runs horizontally across the frame. A workman in a high-visibility vest and white hard hat, seen in profile, puts his weight on the first tread of a short flight of new pine steps at the front of the platform, bounces once to test it, nods to himself, steps down and walks out of frame to the left at an ordinary pace. The camera is locked off on a tripod and does not move at all: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no drift, no handheld shake. Real-time speed, natural human movement, never slow motion. The row of folding chairs and the podium on the platform stay perfectly still; behind them City Hall with its mauve banner; parked cars do not move; the lumber truck and box van stand at the kerb; steam from a hot-food cart; a bus stopped at the far corner. The stage, its steps and the podium remain in the frame in exactly the same place from the first frame to the last; the camera never pans to follow the workman - he simply leaves the frame. A heavy flat overcast, sheet-cake grey sky, no sun and no shadows; a light steady drizzle falls, fine rain visible against the dark stone, the granite paving wet with shallow puddles mirroring the grey sky; street lamps and windows glow warm and are doubled in the wet. On the far street beyond the square and along the side kerbs a few cars move slowly and steadily with their headlights and tail-lights on, reflected in the wet road, at an unhurried city pace - no car ever enters the square or comes near the stage. Prestige political drama photographed on an Arri Alexa with anamorphic lenses: flat overcast daylight, slight 35mm film grain, colours desaturated about twelve percent, warm tungstens, deep browns and charcoals in the shadows, photographic realism.
